title: Total Hom precomposition preserves cochain homotopies
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $P,R,T$ cochain complexes of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the total Hom complexes $H_P=\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,T)$ and $H_R=\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(R,T)$ with differential $D\varphi=d_T\varphi-(-1)^j\varphi d$ on a homogeneous cochain of degree $j$ [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. For a degree-zero chain map $f:P\to R$, the maps $f^*:H_R\to H_P$, $f^*(\varphi)=\varphi f$, are chain maps, with $(1_P)^*=1_{H_P}$ and $(gf)^*=f^*g^*$ for every further cochain complex $L$ and chain map $g:R\to L$, where all Hom targets are $T$. Suppose $f,f':P\to R$ and maps $h^i:P^i\to R^{i-1}$ satisfy $f-f'=d_Rh+hd_P$ (a cochain homotopy). Then the degree-minus-one map $S_h:H_R\to H_P$ specified on a homogeneous degree-$j$ cochain by $S_h(\varphi)=(-1)^j\varphi h$ satisfies
$$f^*-(f')^*=D S_h+S_hD.$$
In particular, for $T=A[0]$, dualization $P^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,A[0])$ sends homotopic maps to homotopic maps. If $f:P\to R$ and $g:R\to P$ are homotopy inverses, then $f^\vee:R^\vee\to P^\vee$ and $g^\vee:P^\vee\to R^\vee$ are homotopy inverses.

source.place: Final two sentences: transport of duality along an isomorphism; the Hom-precomposition homotopy argument needed to dualize a homotopy equivalence.

proof.text: For a homogeneous cochain $\varphi\in H_R^j$, precomposition gives $(f^*\varphi)=\varphi f$. Since $f$ commutes with differentials, $d_Rf=fd_P$, and the total Hom differential is $D\varphi=d_T\varphi-(-1)^j\varphi d_R$, we have $D(\varphi f)=(D\varphi)f$. Thus $f^*$ is a degree-zero chain map.

source.place: Final two sentences: the Hom-precomposition homotopy argument needed to dualize a homotopy equivalence.

proof.text: Precomposition by the identity is the identity on every homogeneous cochain. For composable degree-zero chain maps $P\xrightarrow{f}R\xrightarrow{g}L$ and any cochain $\varphi:L\to T$, $(f^*(g^*\varphi))=(\varphi g)f=\varphi(gf)=(gf)^*\varphi$. Hence $(1_P)^*=1_{H_P}$ and $(gf)^*=f^*g^*$.

source.place: Final two sentences: the Hom-precomposition homotopy argument needed to dualize a homotopy equivalence.

proof.text: Let $h$ have degree $-1$ and define $S_h(\varphi)=(-1)^j\varphi h$ for $\varphi$ homogeneous of degree $j$. The two terms in $DS_h(\varphi)+S_hD(\varphi)$ are $(-1)^j d_T\varphi h+\varphi h d_P$ and $(-1)^{j+1}d_T\varphi h+\varphi d_Rh$, respectively. The $d_T$ terms cancel, leaving $\varphi(hd_P+d_Rh)=\varphi(f-f')=(f^*-(f')^*)\varphi$. Therefore $f^*-(f')^*=DS_h+S_hD$.

source.place: Final two sentences: the Hom-precomposition homotopy argument needed to dualize a homotopy equivalence.

proof.text: Taking $T=A[0]$ gives the stated dual complexes $P^\vee$ and $R^\vee$, and the preceding identity says that a chain homotopy $f\simeq f'$ induces a chain homotopy $f^\vee\simeq(f')^\vee$ via $S_h$.

source.place: Final two sentences: transport of duality along an isomorphism; the Hom-precomposition homotopy argument needed to dualize a homotopy equivalence.

proof.text: If $f:P\to R$ and $g:R\to P$ are homotopy inverses, then $gf\simeq1_P$ and $fg\simeq1_R$. By the previous specialization, $(gf)^*\simeq(1_P)^*$ and $(fg)^*\simeq(1_R)^*$. Using the composition identity, these are $f^\vee g^\vee\simeq1_{P^\vee}$ and $g^\vee f^\vee\simeq1_{R^\vee}$, so $f^\vee$ and $g^\vee$ are homotopy inverses.
